shared_context.condition: untreated chlamydia may not resolve on its own and can cause permanent reproductive damage

atoms.1: Chlamydia trachomatis infections often do not resolve on their own.
atoms.2: Chlamydia trachomatis infections can cause permanent damage if left untreated.
atoms.3: Some bacterial infections may occasionally resolve without treatment.
atoms.4: It is not typical for chlamydia to resolve without treatment.
atoms.5: Most women with genital tract chlamydial infections are asymptomatic.
atoms.6: Asymptomatic nature of genital tract chlamydial infections makes it more challenging to diagnose and treat promptly.
atoms.7: Untreated chlamydia can lead to severe reproductive complications.
atoms.8: Untreated chlamydia can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease.
atoms.9: Untreated chlamydia can lead to tubal factor infertility.
atoms.10: Untreated chlamydia can lead to ectopic pregnancy.
atoms.11: Chlamydia trachomatis has evolved mechanisms to evade the host immune system.
atoms.12: Chlamydia trachomatis can persist within host epithelial cells.
atoms.13: Spontaneous resolution of chlamydia trachomatis infections is unlikely due to its mechanisms of evading the host immune system.

snippets.output: Chlamydia trachomatis has evolved mechanisms to evade the host immune system and can persist within host epithelial cells, making spontaneous resolution unlikely.
Most women with genital tract chlamydial infections are asymptomatic, making it more challenging to diagnose and treat promptly.
Untreated chlamydia can lead to severe reproductive complications, including pelvic inflammatory disease, tubal factor infertility, and ectopic pregnancy.

Chlamydia trachomatis infections often do not resolve on their own and can cause permanent reproductive damage if left untreated, although some bacterial infections may occasionally resolve without treatment.
